content.text:
I fixed the bug: a block scalar whose body is only whitespace now ends at the next less-indented line, and every case in the report loads correctly.

**Cause:** In `readBlockScalar` (`src/parser/parser.ts`, around line 712), the parser remembers the most-indented blank line it has seen before the first content line. YAML forbids those blank lines being more indented than the first content line, so the parser raised "bad indentation of a mapping entry" for the next non-blank line. It did this without first checking whether that line belongs to the scalar at all. In your examples, `    - type: array` and `  y: 1` are at or below the parent's indent, so they end the scalar rather than being part of it.

**Fix:** The check now raises an error only when the line is indented more than the parent, meaning it really is the scalar's first content line. Otherwise the scalar ends there and its body is just the blank lines. With the 8-space line from the report:
- `|+` and `>+` give `"\n"`, matching 4.3.2 and `yaml` 2.9.1.
- `|`, `>` and `|-` give `""`.

The real error is still raised, for example for `a: |\n    \n  x\n`.

**Tests:** I added `test/core/units/block-scalar-blank-body.test.mjs`. It covers `|+`, `>+`, `|`, `>` and `|-` in both layouts from the report (the sequence entry and the sibling key), plus the cases that must still fail. The core suite (`node --test "test/core/**/*.test.mjs"`) gives 324 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped, and `dist/` is rebuilt with the fix.

**Not run:**
- **YAML spec suite (`test/spec`):** it needs `npm run spec:get` to download its test data, which needs the network.
- **ESLint and type-check:** the commands were denied permission, so lint and type-check were not run.

result:
I fixed the bug: a block scalar whose body is only whitespace now ends at the next less-indented line, and every case in the report loads correctly.

**Cause:** In `readBlockScalar` (`src/parser/parser.ts`, around line 712), the parser remembers the most-indented blank line it has seen before the first content line. YAML forbids those blank lines being more indented than the first content line, so the parser raised "bad indentation of a mapping entry" for the next non-blank line. It did this without first checking whether that line belongs to the scalar at all. In your examples, `    - type: array` and `  y: 1` are at or below the parent's indent, so they end the scalar rather than being part of it.

**Fix:** The check now raises an error only when the line is indented more than the parent, meaning it really is the scalar's first content line. Otherwise the scalar ends there and its body is just the blank lines. With the 8-space line from the report:
- `|+` and `>+` give `"\n"`, matching 4.3.2 and `yaml` 2.9.1.
- `|`, `>` and `|-` give `""`.

The real error is still raised, for example for `a: |\n    \n  x\n`.

**Tests:** I added `test/core/units/block-scalar-blank-body.test.mjs`. It covers `|+`, `>+`, `|`, `>` and `|-` in both layouts from the report (the sequence entry and the sibling key), plus the cases that must still fail. The core suite (`node --test "test/core/**/*.test.mjs"`) gives 324 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped, and `dist/` is rebuilt with the fix.

**Not run:**
- **YAML spec suite (`test/spec`):** it needs `npm run spec:get` to download its test data, which needs the network.
- **ESLint and type-check:** the commands were denied permission, so lint and type-check were not run.
